newsitem.title: USA: Ex-members confident suicide cult right about UFO.
newsitem.headline: Ex-members confident suicide cult right about UFO.

text.p: Two ex-members of the UFO cult which committed mass suicide in California last week said on Sunday they were confident the group had beamed up to a spaceship as their leader had promised.

Wayne Cooke, whose wife Suzanne Sylvia Cooke was one of the 39 people who killed themselves in a mansion outside San Diego, said on CBS "60 Minutes" programme he wished he had had the courage to follow suit.

"I think she's probably on another (space) craft somewhere out there," Cooke said of his wife, who like other Heaven's Gate cultists ate drug-laced pudding or applesauce, washed it down with vodka and put a plastic bag over her head to die.

"I wish I had the strength to have remained to have gained the kind of control through Do's help, and Ti's help, to have stuck it out and gotten stronger and continued to be a part of that crew," Cooke said.

"Do" was the cult name for leader Marshall Applewhite, who with partner "Ti" -- a nurse who died in 1985 -- came up with the theory that the group's spirits would be picked up by a spaceship following comet Hale Bopp to Earth.

Both Cooke, who said he joined and left Heaven's Gate several times, and another former member identified only as "Sawyer" interviewed on CBS, had nothing but good words for a cult whose deaths have shocked the world.

Sawyer said he once believed in Applewhite's message of renouncing human ties and corporeal distractions to the point that he considered emulating the former music teacher and voluntarily castrating himself.
"I wanted to very badly at the time," said Sawyer, who eventually opted against the procedure. "I flipped a coin, I lost -- as far as the castration (goes)."
Kelly Cooke, who was abandoned by her parents when they left to join Applewhite in the 1970's, told CBS she respected her mother's wishes.

"I don't believe she committed suicide. That's a strong word to use," Kelly Cooke said. "This was something she worked all of her life to accomplish. She graduated to the next level ... that is enough for me to let her go with peace."
Her father Wayne Cooke said he believed that the cult's spectacular mass suicide had been orchestrated from outer space to draw attention to the group's beliefs.

"They left when a comet came. A comet has significance, historically. They left in the Easter Week. That has significance historically. They left by laying down their bodies, that has enormous impact. Obviously a stage is being set by the next level for this world, for others, to examine this."
